title: Automatic mutual recognition of occupational registrations (Victoria)
summary: Victoria adopted the amended Commonwealth Mutual Recognition Act so interstate-registered workers are deemed registered in Victoria; started 1 July 2021 with a limited set of occupations, with temporary exemptions for real estate agents and professional engineers lifted from 1 January 2022.

instruments.title: Mutual Recognition Amendment Act 2021
instruments.provisions: Amends Mutual Recognition Act 1992 to insert automatic deemed registration (Part 3A)

instruments.title: Mutual Recognition (Victoria) Amendment Act 2021
instruments.provisions: Adopts the Commonwealth AMR amendments for Victoria

instruments.title: Mutual Recognition (Victoria) (Temporary Exemptions) Amendment Declaration (repeal of temporary exemptions, Dec 2021)
instruments.provisions: Repealed temporary exemptions for real estate agents/representatives and professional engineers from 1 Jan 2022

commenced.what: Temporary exemptions for real estate agents and professional engineers repealed

direction_rationale: Removes the need for a separate application and fee to work interstate, lowering the cost of entry for licensed tradespeople and agents from other participating jurisdictions; expected to increase the number of potential suppliers, especially near borders.
comparison: Queensland (never joined) and later-joining states (TAS Dec 2021, SA Feb 2022, WA Jul 2022); border vs non-border regions
confounders: occupation-specific temporary exemptions in each jurisdiction
price_series: Maintenance and repair of the dwelling; Real estate services are not a separate CPI class

Primary commencement chosen on 15 October 2026 as the date the change described in the title took effect; confirm on review.

assessment.summary: Lets tradespeople, real estate agents and other licensed workers registered in one participating state work in another without applying or paying again. A modest gain for labour mobility and for a national market in licensed services; there is little evidence yet on its size.

marks.reason: Removes the application and fee a licensed worker needed before working across the border.
Recognises other participating jurisdictions' registrations, moving towards one national market for licensed services.

assessment.confidence_note: Ex ante analysis only; the scheme's own evaluation is pending, and the Productivity Commission found national licensing may not significantly lift productivity. Queensland does not take part.

responsible.note: The Treasurer administers the Mutual Recognition (Victoria) Act 1998.
Administers Parts 3 and 3A of the Mutual Recognition Act 1992 (automatic mutual recognition).
